:question/problem:
Find the fundamental vector product of the surface defined by the equations 

$$
x=u,\,y=v,\,z={u}^{2}-{v}^{2}.
$$
:question/worked-solution:
For a surface with parametrization $r(u,v),$ the fundamental vector product is defined as ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}.$

In vector form, our surface has the equation 

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u,\,v,\,{u}^{2}-{v}^{2}⟩.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}({u}^{2}-{v}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,2u⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}({u}^{2}-{v}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,-2v⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =\begin{vmatrix}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & 2u \\ 0 & 1 & -2v\end{vmatrix} \\  & =⟨\begin{vmatrix}0 & 2u \\ 1 & -2v\end{vmatrix},\,-\begin{vmatrix}1 & 2u \\ 0 & -2v\end{vmatrix},\,\begin{vmatrix}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{vmatrix}⟩ \\  & =⟨-2u,\,2v,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

:question/problem:
Find the fundamental vector product of the surface defined by the equations 

$$
x=u,\,y=v,\,z=u-{e}^{v}.
$$
:question/worked-solution:
For a surface with parametrization $r(u,v),$ the fundamental vector product is defined as ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}.$

In vector form, our surface has the equation 

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u,\,v,\,u-{e}^{v}⟩.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u-{e}^{v})⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,1⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u-{e}^{v})⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,-{e}^{v}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =\begin{vmatrix}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -{e}^{v}\end{vmatrix} \\  & =⟨\begin{vmatrix}0 & 1 \\ 1 & -{e}^{v}\end{vmatrix},\,-\begin{vmatrix}1 & 1 \\ 0 & -{e}^{v}\end{vmatrix},\,\begin{vmatrix}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{vmatrix}⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,\,{e}^{v},\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

:question/problem:
Find the fundamental vector product of the surface defined by the equations 

$$
x={u}^{2}+1,\,y={v}^{3}+1,\,z=2u+v.
$$
:question/worked-solution:
For a surface with parametrization $r(u,v),$ the fundamental vector product is defined as ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}.$

In vector form, our surface has the equation 

$$
r(u,v)=⟨{u}^{2}+1,\,{v}^{3}+1,\,2u+v⟩.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}({u}^{2}+1),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}({v}^{3}+1),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(2u+v)⟩ \\  & =⟨2u,\,0,\,2⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}({u}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}({v}^{3}+1),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(2u+v)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,3{v}^{2},\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =\begin{vmatrix}i & j & k \\ 2u & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 3{v}^{2} & 1\end{vmatrix} \\  & =⟨\begin{vmatrix}0 & 2 \\ 3{v}^{2} & 1\end{vmatrix},\,-\begin{vmatrix}2u & 2 \\ 0 & 1\end{vmatrix},\,\begin{vmatrix}2u & 0 \\ 0 & 3{v}^{2}\end{vmatrix}⟩ \\  & =⟨-6{v}^{2},\,-2u,\,6u{v}^{2}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

:question/problem: Find the fundamental vector product of the surface generated by the vector-valued function $r(u,v)=⟨u,\,u\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,v\operatorname{cos}⁡u⟩.$
:question/worked-solution:
For a surface with parametrization $r(u,v),$ the fundamental vector product is defined as ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}.$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u\operatorname{sin}⁡v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v\operatorname{cos}⁡u)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,-v\operatorname{sin}⁡u⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u\operatorname{sin}⁡v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v\operatorname{cos}⁡u)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,u\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡u⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =\begin{vmatrix}i & j & k \\ 1 & \operatorname{sin}⁡v & -v\operatorname{sin}⁡u \\ 0 & u\operatorname{cos}⁡v & \operatorname{cos}⁡u\end{vmatrix} \\  & =⟨\begin{vmatrix}\operatorname{sin}⁡v & -v\operatorname{sin}⁡u \\ u\operatorname{cos}⁡v & \operatorname{cos}⁡u\end{vmatrix},\,-\begin{vmatrix}1 & -v\operatorname{sin}⁡u \\ 0 & \operatorname{cos}⁡u\end{vmatrix},\,\begin{vmatrix}1 & \operatorname{sin}⁡v \\ 0 & u\operatorname{cos}⁡v\end{vmatrix}⟩ \\  & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡u\operatorname{sin}⁡v+uv\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡u,\,u\operatorname{cos}⁡v⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

:question/problem: Find the fundamental vector product of the surface generated by the vector-valued function $r(u,v)=⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡u,\,{v}^{2},\,4v\operatorname{cos}⁡u⟩.$
:question/worked-solution:
For a surface with parametrization $r(u,v),$ the fundamental vector product is defined as ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}.$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(\operatorname{sin}⁡u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}({v}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(4v\operatorname{cos}⁡u)⟩ \\  & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡u,\,0,\,-4v\operatorname{sin}⁡u⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(\operatorname{sin}⁡u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}({v}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(4v\operatorname{cos}⁡u)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,2v,\,4\operatorname{cos}⁡u⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =\begin{vmatrix}i & j & k \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡u & 0 & -4v\operatorname{sin}⁡u \\ 0 & 2v & 4\operatorname{cos}⁡u\end{vmatrix} \\  & =⟨\begin{vmatrix}0 & -4v\operatorname{sin}⁡u \\ 2v & 4\operatorname{cos}⁡u\end{vmatrix},\,-\begin{vmatrix}\operatorname{cos}⁡u & -4v\operatorname{sin}⁡u \\ 0 & 4\operatorname{cos}⁡u\end{vmatrix},\,\begin{vmatrix}\operatorname{cos}⁡u & 0 \\ 0 & 2v\end{vmatrix}⟩ \\  & =⟨8{v}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡u,\,-4{cos}^{2}⁡u,\,2v\operatorname{cos}⁡u⟩.\end{aligned}
$$
